thread:
maria (PM): Quick sync - we need a concise gating spec for new catalog entries that makes migration costs explicit. Goal: fewer surprise tickets during deprecations and a clear path for pin requests.

ashok (Eng): +1. Minimal gates I propose: performance bench, quantization compatibility, and a rolling-upgrade test. Also add an explicit `status` flag: experimental | stable | deprecated.

liz (ML): For benchmarks: keep it lightweight. Two short checks: an E2E latency bench (p50/p99) and a small regression harness (<=100 curated prompts). Makes onboarding < 1 day for smaller models.

ashok (Eng): Draft thresholds: p99 delta <= 20ms vs baseline on identical seq workloads; quality regression < 2% on the mini-harness. If either fails, mark `status=experimental`.

maria (PM): Add a cost metric too: infer cost per 1k tokens change <= 1.3x baseline to be considered for automatic pin removal.

jen (Sales): From customer calls: customers will tolerate small perf/quality deltas if we provide tooling + a 30-day grace. They also want a paid option to keep old model pinned long-term.

ashok (Eng): Implementation idea: catalog entry has fields: status, compat_layers, pin_policy. runtime consults pin_policy during routing. Example in-line: ```json
{
  "model":"xyz-13b",
  "status":"stable",
  "pin_policy":"manual",
  "compat_layers":true
}
```

liz (ML): Note: `compat_layers` implies maintenance (tokenizer/IO shims, adapter fixes) and ~2-4 engineer-weeks per major family. Must be captured in onboarding cost estimates.

derek (CS): Support needs a customer-facing migration template: timeline, behavior diffs, rollback steps, curl example with pin header. Console should expose a one-click toggle to stay on the old model during testing.

sam (SRE): Ops constraint: many orgs pinning large models hurts capacity planning. Two options: paid dedicated pin pool or soft eviction with advance warnings. I prefer paid pool for predictable capacity accounting.

maria (PM): Proposal: two lanes - (1) free short pins (30 days, limited concurrent per org, auto-expire), (2) paid long-term pins (SLA + dedicated capacity). Document in catalog entry and pricing page.

jen (Sales): If we ship a clear paid pin product, enterprise uptake will follow. Recommend discount tiers for annual commitments.

ashok (Eng): Rollout plan: phase 0 = catalog metadata + console pin toggle; phase 1 = bench harness + onboarding checklist; phase 2 = paid pin infra and dedicated pool. Estimate: 6 sprints to full.

liz (ML): Can we enable A/B migrations? Runtime should support routing splits (e.g., 5/95) and add per-prompt annotations to enable automatic quality checks during canary.

maria (PM): Launch gates: (a) bench pass, (b) <=1% regression on customer-flagged prompts during canary, (c) automated rollback if >2% error spike. These are hard gates for default catalog mutations.

derek (CS): I'll draft the customer migration template and support playbook. Need a canary-run checklist.

ashok (Eng): I'll open a PR for schema changes and a minimal routing change. Tagging @liz @sam for review.

canary-bot: canary/xyz-13b warmed and passed warmup. CI link: https://ci/internal/2423

maria (PM): Next actions: Derek + Jen to produce customer comms and pricing spec by EOD Friday; Ashok + Liz to land schema PR + benchmark harness prototype by next Wed; Sam to sketch capacity model for paid pin pool. I will consolidate into a roadmap ticket after PRs land.

jen (Sales): FYI two customers already asked for multi-month pins. I'll collect contract language examples and share.

ashok (Eng): Local bench command: ```bash
./bench/run.sh --model xyz-13b --seq 512 --iters 200
```

maria (PM): Thanks all. Reconvene in product sync next Tue. :rocket:
